title: Prime-power roots have epimorphic power transitions
statement:
For any scheme S on which l is invertible in every residue field, the canonical l-th-power transition from the roots of order l^(n+2) to the roots of order l^(n+1) [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf] is an epimorphism for every natural n.

theorem purTwistRootTransitions_epi (S : Scheme.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    [∀ x : S, Invertible (l : S.residueField x)] (n : ℕ) :
    Epi (proEtaleRootsOfUnityTransition S (l ^ (n + 1)) (l ^ (n + 2))
      (pow_pos (Fact.out : l.Prime).pos _) (pow_pos (Fact.out : l.Prime).pos _)
      (pow_dvd_pow l (Nat.le_succ (n + 1))))

source.place: Coefficient-twist blueprint proof step 2; Stacks Tag 03PK.

proof.text: Invertibility in residue fields implies invertibility in stalks and global sections. On every test scheme apply the Kummer cover theorem to a unit of order l^(n+1). Its local l-th root has order dividing l^(n+2). The canonical sectionwise kernel identification supplies a section upstairs. Naturality of the inclusion into units and the normalized transition formula show that it maps to the original section. The etale covering is a pro-etale covering, giving local surjectivity. Use the sheaf epi criterion.
